questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa), named after Blaise Pascal. 1 Pa = 1 N/m?.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the principle behind the working of a hydraulic lift?
questions.explanation: A hydraulic lift works on Pascal's Law, which states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of lens is used to correct myopia (near-sightedness)?
questions.explanation: Myopia (near-sightedness) is corrected using a concave lens (diverging lens), which spreads out light rays before they enter the eye.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the work done when a force of 10 N moves an object by 5 m in the direction of force?
questions.explanation: Work = Force ? Displacement = 10 ? 5 = 50 J.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is a non-contact force as it acts without physical contact between objects. Friction, tension and normal force are contact forces.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the wavelength of a wave with frequency 50 Hz and speed 340 m/s?
questions.explanation: Wavelength (?) = Speed (v) / Frequency (f) = 340 / 50 = 6.8 m.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of sulphuric acid?
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid has the chemical formula H?SO?. It is a strong mineral acid widely used in industry.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen (N?) is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere, comprising about 78% of the air.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the process of converting a solid directly into a gas called?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the process in which a solid directly changes into a gas without passing through the liquid state. Dry ice (solid CO?) undergoes sublimation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Silver is the best conductor of electricity among all metals. Copper is the second best and most commonly used.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the atomic number of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has atomic number 8, which means it has 8 protons in its nucleus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the human brain is responsible for thinking and memory?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for higher functions like thinking, memory, speech, and voluntary movement.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which organ in the human body produces bile?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the small intestine to help digest fats.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the normal blood pressure of a healthy adult human?
questions.explanation: The normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is approximately 120/80 mm Hg. 120 is systolic pressure and 80 is diastolic pressure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a deficiency disease?
questions.explanation: Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency. Malaria, tuberculosis and cholera are infectious diseases caused by pathogens.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which organelle is known as the 'suicidal bag' of the cell?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are known as the 'suicidal bags' of the cell because they contain digestive enzymes that can break down the cell's own components when damaged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which disease is caused by the bite of an Anopheles mosquito?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, which is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the plant conducts water from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem tissue transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves in plants. It is composed of tracheids and vessels.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another called?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one transparent medium to another due to a change in its speed.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Helium (He) is a noble gas in Group 18 of the periodic table. Noble gases are generally unreactive due to their full valence shells.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for the absorption of calcium in the body?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium from the intestines. Deficiency of Vitamin D can lead to weak bones and rickets.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the formula for kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy (KE) = ?mv?, where m is mass and v is velocity of the object.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which acid is found in lemon and orange?
questions.explanation: Citric acid is found in citrus fruits like lemon, orange, and grapefruit. It gives these fruits their sour taste.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which is the largest artery in the human body?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the largest artery in the human body. It carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle of the heart to the rest of the body.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the reason for the formation of a rainbow?
questions.explanation: A rainbow is formed due to the refraction, dispersion, and internal reflection of sunlight by water droplets in the atmosphere.

questions.question: In an election, the winning candidate got 60% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 4000 votes. How many valid votes were cast?
questions.explanation: Difference = 60% - 40% = 20% of total votes = 4000 ? Total = 4000/0.20 = 20000.

questions.explanation: Let CP = x. SP1 = 0.85x, SP2 = 1.1x. Difference = 1.1x - 0.85x = 0.25x = 75 ? x = 300.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A man walks at 6 km/h for 4 hours and then at 8 km/h for 3 hours. What is his average speed?
questions.explanation: Total distance = (6?4) + (8?3) = 24 + 24 = 48 km. Total time = 4 + 3 = 7 h. Average speed = 48/7 = 6.86 km/h.

questions.explanation: 33 is a composite number as it has factors 3 and 11. 19, 23 and 29 are prime numbers.

questions.explanation: Area = ? ? base ? height = ? ? 12 ? 8 = 48 cm?.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle of length 15 cm and breadth 10 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 2(15 + 10) = 2 ? 25 = 50 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the value of sin? 30? + cos? 30??
questions.explanation: sin? ? + cos? ? = 1 (fundamental trigonometric identity). So sin? 30? + cos? 30? = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 25. If three numbers 20, 25 and 30 are removed, what is the new average?
questions.explanation: Sum of 8 numbers = 8 ? 25 = 200. Remaining sum = 200 - 20 - 25 - 30 = 125. New average = 125/5 = 25.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 32. What is the sum of the numbers?
questions.explanation: Sum = Average ? Number of items = 32 ? 5 = 160.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of the angles of a pentagon is:
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of a polygon = (n - 2) ? 180? where n is the number of sides. For pentagon, n = 5. Sum = (5 - 2) ? 180? = 3 ? 180? = 540?.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of the angles of a hexagon is:
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of a polygon = (n - 2) ? 180?. For hexagon, n = 6. Sum = (6 - 2) ? 180? = 4 ? 180? = 720?.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term: Teacher : School :: Doctor : ?
questions.explanation: A teacher works in a school. Similarly, a doctor works in a hospital.

questions.explanation: Banana, Mango and Apple are fruits. Carrot is a vegetable.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a boy, a woman said, "He is the son of my father's only daughter." How is that boy related to the woman?
questions.explanation: Father's only daughter = the woman herself (if she is the only daughter). Her son = the woman's son. So the boy is her son.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Introducing a girl, a man said, "She is the daughter of my mother's only brother." How is that girl related to the man?
questions.explanation: Mother's only brother = Maternal uncle. His daughter = the man's cousin (maternal cousin).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A woman walks 10 km towards East. She turns right and walks 5 km. She then turns right and walks 10 km. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 10 km East ? turns right (South) 5 km ? turns right (West) 10 km. Net displacement = 5 km South. So distance = 5 km.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A man starts from point P and walks 6 km towards North. He turns left and walks 8 km. He then turns left and walks 6 km. In which direction is he from point P?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 6 km North ? turns left (West) 8 km ? turns left (South) 6 km. Net displacement = 8 km West. So he is in West direction.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All books are novels. Some novels are comics. Conclusions: I. Some books are comics. II. Some novels are books. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: All books are novels implies some novels are books (II follows). But some novels are comics does not mean some books are comics (I does not follow).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers. Conclusions: I. All pens are erasers. II. Some erasers are pencils. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: All pens are pencils and all pencils are erasers ? All pens are erasers (I follows). Also, all pencils are erasers implies some erasers are pencils (II follows).

questions.question: In a group of 180 people, 120 like pizza, 90 like burger, and 50 like both. How many like only pizza?
questions.explanation: Only pizza = Total pizza - Both = 120 - 50 = 70.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In a class of 90 students, 50 like cricket, 40 like hockey, and 10 like neither. How many like both?
questions.explanation: Students liking at least one = 90 - 10 = 80. Both = 50 + 40 - 80 = 10.

questions.explanation: When mirror is on the right, the word appears reversed laterally. APPLE ? reverse: ELPPA ? flip each: E??, L??, P??, P??, A?A. So ????A.

options: Both I and II are implicit

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773-1785). He was appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Jallianwala Bagh Massacre' took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919, when British troops fired on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first Indian to become the Governor-General of India?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari was the first and last Indian Governor-General of India, serving from 1948 to 1950.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Executive?
questions.explanation: Part V of the Indian Constitution (Articles 52 to 151) deals with the Union Executive, which includes the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, and Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The concept of 'Concurrent List' is borrowed from which country's constitution?
questions.explanation: The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Australian Constitution. It contains subjects on which both the Centre and States can legislate.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The President of India can be removed from office by?
questions.explanation: The President of India can be removed from office through impeachment by Parliament for violation of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Ganga of the South'?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is known as the 'Ganga of the South' because it is the longest river in South India and has a large basin.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Gateway of India' is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Gateway of India is a historic monument located in Mumbai, built in 1924 to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Tropic of Cancer' does NOT pass through which state?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. It does NOT pass through Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax in India?
questions.explanation: Income tax is a direct tax, as it is levied directly on the income of individuals and corporations. GST, excise duty, and sales tax are indirect taxes.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'RBI' was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Finance Commission' is constituted every?
questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the President of India under Article 280 of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for the 'fight or flight' response?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is responsible for the 'fight or flight' response. It is released by the adrenal glands during stress or danger.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the pH of saliva in the human mouth?
questions.explanation: The pH of human saliva is approximately 6.5 (slightly acidic to neutral). It helps in the digestion of starch.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is a renewable source of energy as it is continuously available and does not get depleted. Coal, petroleum, and natural gas are non-renewable.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The book 'A Suitable Boy' is written by?
questions.explanation: A Suitable Boy' is a novel by Vikram Seth, published in 1993. It is one of the longest novels in English literature.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The autobiography 'Wings of Fire' is written by?
questions.explanation: Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, the former President of India, co-authored with Arun Tiwari.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian cricketer is known as 'Mr. 360'?
questions.explanation: AB de Villiers is known as 'Mr. 360' for his ability to play shots in all directions around the wicket. He is a South African cricketer.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The term 'Grand Slam' in tennis refers to winning which number of major titles in a calendar year?
questions.explanation: In tennis, a Grand Slam refers to winning all four major tournaments (Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open) in the same calendar year.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The first Indian to win a medal in individual event at the Olympics is?
questions.explanation: K.D. Jadhav was the first Indian to win an individual medal at the Olympics, winning a bronze medal in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Ajanta Caves' are located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Ajanta Caves are located in Maharashtra. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and are known for their ancient Buddhist rock-cut cave paintings.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Elephanta Caves' are located on which island?
questions.explanation: The Elephanta Caves are located on Elephanta Island in Mumbai Harbour, Maharashtra. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which day is celebrated as 'National Youth Day' in India?
questions.explanation: National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January every year in India to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which day is celebrated as 'National Science Day' in India?
questions.explanation: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February every year to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman in 1928.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is the current President of India as of 2026?
questions.explanation: Droupadi Murmu is the current President of India (as of 2026), having assumed office on 25 July 2022. She is the first tribal woman to hold this position.
